# Mode S extended squitter

Two DF17 aircraft-identification messages, pulse-position modulated at 1 Mbit/s,
2.4 MS/s complex on 1090 MHz. Three kilobytes, because Mode S is 112 bits and 112 bits
at a megabit is 112 microseconds.

**Nobody transmitted this and no aircraft exists.** It is generated by
`fixtures/make.mjs` from a fixed seed. The ICAO addresses are `4840D6` (the address
used in every Mode S worked example ever written) and `ABCDEF`; the callsigns are
`SDRFLEX` and `SDRFLX2`. Both frames carry a correct 24-bit parity, computed by the
generator with the Mode S polynomial, which is what lets dump1090 accept them —
a fixture that dump1090 rejects would be testing nothing.
